narrative.overview:
A Lebanese cement-tile floor: a deep teal shell laid over cool limestone, white surfaces set into it like inlays, and tile motifs doing the work other apps give to icon sets and progress bars. Every category owns a geometric tile and a tile colour; every budget is a row of cells that fill.

Two hues carry meaning and are rationed. Marigold marks the one thing you can do next. Oxblood-red marks over-budget and nothing else, and never travels without an icon and words. English and Arabic share one family (Readex Pro); layout is logical-property only.
keyCharacteristics: Teal shell block at the top of a screen, limestone ground, white card inlays with 1px grout borders.
Eight tile motifs in three tile colours (teal, oxblood, ochre) as category identity.
Progress is tile cells (16 per bar), never a smooth fill.
Flat: depth comes from tonal layering and borders, almost no shadow.
One typeface, five sizes, tabular figures for money.
Dark theme exists but is provisional.

rules.name: The One Next Thing Rule
rules.body: Marigold appears only on the Add action. Nothing else on a screen may be marigold.

rules.name: The Change-Only Alert Rule
rules.body: Oxblood-red means over-budget. Never decoration, never a generic error colour, never colour alone: icon plus text every time.

rules.name: The Tile Colour Rule
rules.body: Teal, oxblood and ochre tiles identify categories. A tile in oxblood does not mean over.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every amount uses tabular figures; body text does not.

rules.name: The Flat Inlay Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are set into the ground with borders and tone, never lifted with shadow.

dos: Do use logical utilities only (ms-, pe-, start-, text-start).
Do wrap amounts in Amount and names in <bdi>; keep the keypad and TileBar dir=ltr.
Do pair every oxblood-red use with the triangle-alert icon and the word "Over".
Do keep targets at 44px or more and inputs at 16px or more.
Do reach for a tile motif and tile colour to identify a category.
donts: Don't use marigold anywhere except the Add action and its Save twin.
Don't use oxblood-red for non-budget errors or decoration, or without icon and text.
Don't replace the tile bar with a smooth progress bar, or lead with a hero-metric card.
Don't add or compare USD with LBP in any visual treatment; each currency has its own bar.
Don't treat the dark tokens as final, or the planned tile-pattern band and tile ornament empty state as built (planned for Phase 2, absent from the build).
